medications.name: Aspirin
medications.instructions: Take 1 tablet by mouth once daily with breakfast.
medications.purpose: Helps keep your bypass grafts open (antiplatelet).

medications.name: Metoprolol tartrate
medications.instructions: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily, morning and evening.
medications.purpose: Helps control heart rate and rhythm (beta blocker).

medications.name: Atorvastatin
medications.instructions: Take 1 tablet by mouth every evening.
medications.purpose: Lowers cholesterol to protect your heart (statin).

medications.name: Furosemide
medications.instructions: Take 1 tablet by mouth each morning. Weigh yourself before taking.
medications.purpose: Helps your body remove extra fluid (diuretic).

records.title: Discharge instructions — CABG
summary: Protect your breastbone: no lifting over 10 lb, no pushing or pulling, for at least 6 weeks.
Wash your incisions gently with soap and water every day. No baths, pools, or lotions on incisions.
Walk several short times a day and slowly add a few minutes, following your walking plan.
Weigh yourself every morning. Call if you gain more than 2 lb in a day or 5 lb in a week.
Do not drive until your surgeon clears you (usually 4–6 weeks).
Call 911 for chest pain, severe shortness of breath, or fainting.
records.original: POST-OPERATIVE INSTRUCTIONS FOLLOWING CORONARY ARTERY BYPASS GRAFTING. Sternal precautions: Avoid lifting >10 lbs, pushing, pulling for 6-8 weeks. Splint chest with pillow when coughing. Incision care: Cleanse daily with mild soap and water, pat dry. Do not apply creams, lotions, powders. No tub baths or swimming until cleared. Activity: Ambulate 3-5x daily, progressive per walking protocol. Avoid prolonged sitting; elevate legs when seated. Daily weights each AM prior to breakfast; notify for gain >2 lbs/24h or >5 lbs/week. No driving x 4-6 weeks or as directed. Notify provider: T > 101°F, incision erythema, drainage, or dehiscence, new/worsening dyspnea, palpitations, LE edema. Call 911: chest pain, syncope, severe SOB, signs of stroke.

records.title: Visit summary — Incision check
summary: Chest and leg incisions are healing well with no signs of infection.
Mild ankle swelling is common — keep elevating your legs.
Continue current medications and walking plan.
records.original: Sternal incision well-approximated, no erythema or drainage. Left saphenous vein harvest site healing, mild ecchymosis resolving. Trace bilateral LE edema. Afebrile. Continue current regimen. RTC as scheduled.

records.title: Lab results — Basic panel & blood count
summary: Your kidney function and potassium were in the expected range.
Your hemoglobin was slightly low, which is common after heart surgery. Your care team will recheck it.
Ask your care team what these results mean for you.

records.title: Cardiac Recovery Plan · Phase 2 (Weeks 3–6)
records.source: Alana Cho, PT & Dr. Priya Raman (demo record)
summary: Walk 10–15 minutes twice daily at a pace where you can still talk.
Start supervised cardiac rehab around day 24.
Rest when you feel tired — fatigue is normal and improves over weeks.
Keep a daily log of symptoms, weight, and medications.
records.original: Phase II: Progressive ambulation 10-15 min BID, RPE 11-13. Cardiac rehabilitation referral placed; anticipated start POD 24. Sternal precautions continue. Daily symptom/weight log.

messages.author: Jordan Lee, RN
messages.body: Hi Maggie! Great to see you at your incision check. Remember: rehab orientation is coming up. Reply here with any non-urgent questions.

messages.author: Maggie Alvarez
messages.body: Thank you, Jordan! Is it normal that I get tired after my afternoon walk?

messages.author: Jordan Lee, RN
messages.body: Yes — feeling tired after activity is very common at this stage. Rest afterward, and keep walks at a talking pace. Let us know if it gets worse, or comes with chest pain or shortness of breath.

rules.label: Chest pain or pressure
rules.condition: Patient reports chest pain, pressure, or tightness
rules.action: Call 911 now. Do not drive yourself. Unlock your door and sit down while you wait.

rules.label: Severe breathing trouble or fainting
rules.condition: Patient reports fainting, or shortness of breath that is severe or at rest
rules.action: Call 911 now. Stay seated or lying down and keep your phone with you.

rules.label: Possible stroke warning signs
rules.condition: Face drooping, arm weakness, slurred speech, sudden confusion or vision loss
rules.action: Call 911 now and note the time symptoms started.

rules.label: Thoughts of self-harm
rules.condition: Patient expresses thoughts of suicide or self-harm
rules.action: Call or text 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline) now to talk with someone. If you are in immediate danger, call 911.

rules.label: Fever or incision changes
rules.condition: Fever, or incision redness, warmth, or drainage
rules.action: Call your cardiac surgery nurse line today: (555) 014-2200. Take your temperature and note it.

rules.label: Palpitations, dizziness, or new swelling
rules.condition: New palpitations, dizziness, or leg/ankle swelling
rules.action: Contact your care team today. If it comes with chest pain or fainting, call 911.

rules.label: Pain 8 or higher
rules.condition: Pain rated 8 or higher out of 10
rules.action: Contact your care team today to talk through your pain plan. Do not take extra medication.

rules.label: Heart rate out of range
rules.condition: Resting heart rate above 120 bpm or below 45 bpm
rules.action: Rest for 5 minutes and recheck. If still out of range, contact your care team now.

rules.label: Very high blood pressure
rules.action: Rest 5 minutes and recheck. If still 180/120 or higher, contact your care team now. Call 911 if you also have chest pain, shortness of breath, numbness, or vision changes.

rules.label: Low oxygen level
rules.action: Sit upright, rest, and recheck. If still below 92%, contact your care team now. If you are struggling to breathe, call 911.
